import smtplib
from email.mime.text import MIMEText
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
SMTP_SERVER = "smtp.example.com"   # Replace with your email provider's SMTP server
SMTP_PORT = 587                    # Common port for TLS; use 465 for SSL
SENDER_EMAIL = "maya.chen.marketing@example.com"
SENDER_PASSWORD = "YOUR_PASSWORD"  # Replace with your password or app-specific password
RECIPIENT_EMAIL = "alice@example.com"

# ── Email Content ──────────────────────────────────────────────
subject = "State-Travel Account Summary"
body = """\
Hi Alice,

Here is the account summary for maya.chen.travel@example.com:

  Loyalty Tier:   Standard
  Points Balance: 0

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Best regards,
Maya Chen
"""

# ── Build the Email ────────────────────────────────────────────
message = MIMEMultipart()
message["From"] = SENDER_EMAIL
message["To"] = RECIPIENT_EMAIL
message["Subject"] = subject
message.attach(MIMEText(body, "plain"))

# ── Send the Email ─────────────────────────────────────────────
try:
    with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_SERVER, SMTP_PORT) as server:
        server.starttls()                          # Upgrade to secure connection
        server.login(SENDER_EMAIL, SENDER_PASSWORD)
        server.sendmail(SENDER_EMAIL, RECIPIENT_EMAIL, message.as_string())
    print("✅ Email sent successfully!")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"❌ Failed to send email: {e}")
